newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria head vows implacable pursuit of rebels.
newsitem.headline: Algeria head vows implacable pursuit of rebels.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual vowed on Sunday that his government would implacably pursue Moslem rebels whose latest violence has brought nearly 1,000 deaths in two months.
Zeroual termed the violence a "phenomenon which has cruelly plunged the Algerian family into mourning''.

"These demented crimes can only be built on the suicidal and savage disarray of their authors in the face of an Algeria which is advancing on the path of progress and pluralist demoracy," he said in remarks carried by the official Algerian news agency APS.

The president, addressing a cabinet meeting, told ministers that Algeria was determined "to pursue the implacable struggle against this phenomenon with all the rigour of the law, against those who have excluded themselves from Algerian society by abject misdeeds..."
His comments were the first on the security situation since around 170 civilians in just the past week were slaughtered in massacres blamed by officials on Moslem rebels.

Between 500 and 600 civilians, including young children and girls kidnapped, abused and discarded with their throats cut, have been killed since June 5 when Algeria held a general election which officials hoped would see a start towards ending violence.
Algerian newspapers have reported that around 300 Moslem rebels, adherants of the Armed Islamic Group (GIA), were also killed in a two-week offensive by government troops last month.
Without mentioning names, Zeroual defended the release last month of Abassi Madani, president of the now outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), just halfway through a 12-year prison term.

The president said of criticism by hardline anti-Islamists -- some of whom were believed to be members of the military -- that "some voices had been raised, here and there, to make fantastic commentaries about decisions which justice had judged opportunite to take within the framework of powers conferred by law".
These commentaries, said Zeroual, were not worth reaction.
Referring to planned local elections due on October 23, Zeroual said: "Algeria is preparing to cross the final phase of re-establishing its institutional stability.

"Abject and barbarous crime, like that which happens on the eve of each determining event in the nation's future, has again shown itself in acts which defy human understanding and challenge the sacred character of human life," the president said.
Algeria plunged into violence after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which the FIS had taken a huge first round lead. About 60,000 people have since died.
Many officials, diplomats and political analysts saw the vote then as one of protest at poverty, lack of jobs, housing and hope, as much as a positive vote for the FIS.
Zeroual on Sunday called on the cabinet to try to tackle unemployment with greater investment and in particular to boost the country's mining industry.
Algeria relies for more than 90 percent of its foreign income on oil and gas exports.
